category: debrid link generator with usenet and torrent cloud

free_tier.stated: No free allowance on the paid tiers; the free account is a separate record. The 14-day entry is paid: '14 Days Trial €4.50'.
free_tier.notes: The plan named 'Trial' costs 4.50 EUR, so Deepbrid has no free trial in the sense the other services use the word.

egress.terms: 'Unlimited downloads, unlimited bandwidth' on every paid term, with the footnotes 'Some providers have daily limits' and 'Torrent cloud limited to 50 active slots per user'. No account-wide byte cap is published.

interface_detail: REST API v1 with an apikey; rate limits are per account per minute, shared between key and cookie sessions, and every response carries X-RateLimit-Limit and X-RateLimit-Remaining.
tooling: Documented REST API (including /downloads, /torrents, /usenet, /hosts, /user/limits), browser extensions, WebDAV, Discord and Telegram integrations advertised on the home page.
chaining: One of only three services here that carries usenet, and the cheapest of them at EUR 4.99 for 30 days; with 80+ hosts plus NZB plus a torrent cloud it can replace two subscriptions, as long as the files stay under 200 GB.

binding_note: The account has no byte cap, so the 200 GB per-object limit only fires on very large single files. price_per_tb_month: EUR 4.99 per 30 days, flat; EUR 32.99 per year (EUR 2.75/month)
notes: The annual term at 32.99 EUR is the lowest per-month price of any service - 2.75 EUR - and the reason this record exists separately from the free tier. Candidates for the first failure: the sharing detector firing on a second IP, a per-host daily limit, or a host disappearing. The first two are documented; the third is documented as unrefundable. The vendor's API endpoint was not located, so the error strings for this service are unverified and the record does not claim any. Free tier is a trial in shape, not in name: 5 links a day with reduced host coverage and no named expiry. Abandonment condition: if /api/v1/user/limits starts publishing a free-account byte quota, the request-count binding should be re-checked against it. The only provider in the set with a documented price rise inside the window: the entry term went from EUR 3.99 to EUR 4.50 between 2023-10-26 and 2024-10-02, +12.8%, and has not moved since. The free tier moved the other way in the same period, from 4 to 5 links a day, so what the free user got improved while what the paid user paid rose. The comparison corpus lists EUR 4.99/30 days no pricing page was found at /pricing (404), so the price is not repeated as a verified number here. The contradiction is the finding: the product page sells a cloud the FAQ says does not exist. Until a logged-in account shows a file surviving a session, the conservative vendor statement governs. Abandonment condition: a screenshot of a file in the cloud space after logout would flip this record. The price is the gap. A third-party review claims USD 4.99 and lists 'Credit card payments, Bitcoin, Hysterium, litecoin' - 'Hysterium' is not a coin, which is a fair measure of that source's care, so nothing from it is carried into this record.
